title: Synthetic-probe-driven VPC networking Terraform module
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Deliver a reusable Terraform module that provides production-ready VPC networking for Redwood Private deployments: multi-AZ subnet groups (public/private/isolated), optional NAT Gateway or NAT instance patterns, IGW attachment, comprehensive VPC Endpoint support (S3 Gateway, Interface endpoints for ECR/STS/SecretsManager/KMS/SSM), route tables per subnet tier, IPv6 egress support, and opinionated tagging and IAM endpoint policies. The module must be cloud-agnostic within AWS constraints (assume AWS first) and expose inputs for CIDR plan, AZ distribution, per-subnet sizing strategy, egress pattern (NAT-GW | NAT-Instance | centralized-proxy), endpoint enablement toggles, and route table assignment modes (shared vs per-subnet).

Design goals: idempotent, minimal breaking changes on upgrade, clear outputs for peering/router attachments, and built-in observability hooks. Provide explicit outputs for core resources (vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, nat_gateway_ids, route_table_ids, endpoint_ids). Avoid implicit creation of service-linked roles beyond those required.

Upgrade strategy: support safe in-place updates where possible; for destructive changes (CIDR shrink, subnet replacement), provide a migration helper plan that: 1) creates new subnets and route tables, 2) shifts route associations and ENIs, 3) retires old subnets after traffic verification. Document terraform state migration steps and use a marker tag to coordinate rolling cutover. For NAT Gateway replacements implement a dual-NAT canary pattern: create secondary NAT, switch a small subset of private subnets' route tables to new NAT, run probes, then cutover remaining subnets.

Health checks & observability: embed a synthetic-probing pattern using a small, managed Lambda (or EKS job) that runs cross-AZ connectivity probes every minute: (a) public->private egress via NAT, (b) endpoint-specific checks (S3 Put/Get, ECR token fetch, KMS encrypt/decrypt roundtrip via a test key), and (c) VPC endpoint interface connectivity (TLS handshake). Publish metrics to CloudWatch: endpoint_latency_ms, endpoint_error_rate, nat_gateway_latency_ms, route_table_association_failures, vpc_drift_detected. Provide recommended CloudWatch Alarms and dashboard JSON. Integrate with existing Redwood Console tracing by emitting tags to the observability pipeline and storing probe run logs in a dedicated logging group.

Security & compliance: default endpoint policies restrict to Redwood service principals and customer-account-labeled resources where applicable. Enable option to provision interface endpoints in dedicated subnets with restrictive SGs. KMS integration: allow passing customer-managed KMS key ARN for secrets & logs encryption. Module param security_review_required = true (string) will gate certain changes behind a manual approval workflow in the infra CI pipeline.

Testing & validation: Unit tests with Terratest/localstack for plan/apply/plan idempotence. End-to-end integration in a non-prod sandbox: deploy two VPCs (blue/green) and exercise synthetic probes, fail NAT-GW to validate automatic failover playbook. Provide example pipeline job snippets for GitHub Actions/Concourse showing terraform plan with drift detection, plan cost estimate, and an automated rollout that performs canary route-table swaps.

Deliverables: Terraform module (semantic versioning), README with inputs/outputs and upgrade playbook, example usage modules for single-AZ and multi-AZ deployments, CloudWatch dashboard JSON, Lambda (probe) code reference, CI job templates, runbook for on-call and migration runbook for CIDR/subnet changes.
